newsitem.title: USA: US debt allocations mostly steady Nov 5 wk-survey.
newsitem.headline: US debt allocations mostly steady Nov 5 wk-survey.

text.p: Money managers made minor adjustments to their U.S. debt allocations in the past week, but moved universally toward extension, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates Inc.
"There was again widespread, but generally slight duration extension in this week's survey," the report said. "This week's survey results were very similar to last week's."

In the week ended November 5, the survey's bear/bull index arithmetic reading was at 4.70, up from 4.56 the prior week; the asset-weighted number fell to 4.65, down from 4.79 in the week ended October 29, according to the report.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
The cash/assets ratio fell to 6.93 percent from 6.98 percent.
Duration bogey slipped to 4.11 from 4.12 on an arithmetic basis and fell a modest 4.68 from 4.69 on a weighted basis.
Duration bogey is the level of asset or liability duration sought in the management of a portfolio.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.

Twenty percent of the portfolio managers polled said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from 16 percent the week before. The bear/bull index collected among those intending to be active was 4.80, down from 5.25 the previous week.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
